messages:
Ada: CI perf alert — canary p99 latency jumped ~45% after the model onboarding this morning. Rollout paused, blocking the release. Logs below.

ci-bot: perf-test failed: canary_p99=350ms (baseline 240ms) -> regression +45%. Test: rtv2-small-load-10k

Marco: I pulled the checkpoint diffs. The new checkpoint includes a tokenizer remap (tokenizer_map.json) that reassigns several high-frequency subword ids. That can change tokenization length distribution for long docs.

Sasha: Right — if average sequence length increases, the runtime's kernel selector flips to the slower attention fallback. We have a routing rule: if seq_len > 48 choose fallback_kernel_v1. New tokens may push many requests over that threshold.

Ada: Starting a bisect. Root ts: 1893456789. Initial suspects: model onboarding PR 0f3a9b2 -> tokenizer_map + tokenizer_config tweaks.

Marco: Quick tokenizer diff locally on a sample of 10k web docs:
```
old_avg_tokens: 20
new_avg_tokens: 26
delta: +6 (30% increase)
```
Token examples (old -> new ids):
```
"ing" : 452 -> 9001
" the" : 12 -> 47
```

Sasha: I profiled a representative request on the canary node (cpu+gpu). Short summary:
```
seq_len(before): 22 -> seq_len(after): 29
kv_cache_hit_rate: 72% -> 34%
chosen_kernel: fast_attention_v2 -> fallback_attention_matmul
memcpy_total: 12MB -> 48MB
p99_latency: 240ms -> 350ms
```
Looks like both longer sequences and higher KV misses.

Lee: Hypothesis: token id remap changes chunk boundaries for the tokenizer, breaking locality that KV cache relied on. More misses -> more KV loads -> slower kernel path via route threshold. Also watch for KV key hashing differences if ids changed ordering.

infra-bot: Canary deploy paused by rollout controller — reason: perf-regression. @Ada @Marco @Sasha

Marco: I tried forcing the runtime to prefer fast_attention_v2 (temporary override):
```
RENDER_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=prefer_fast
ROUTE_SEQ_LEN_THRESHOLD=64
```
Local microbench: p99 improved ~30% on sample prompts.

Sasha: Forcing the kernel is a risky correctness override; if model outputs depend on slightly different tokenization ordering, we might get subtle regressions. But as an experiment it's useful.

Ada: Plan options:
- Revert tokenizer remap in the canary to confirm cause (quick rollback)
- Apply route_threshold bump to canary and rerun perf suite (mitigation)
- Work with model team to produce a token-preserving mapping or update KV cache keying

Marco: I opened a revert PR that restores the previous tokenizer_map.json and leaves other onboard changes. Will run e2e perf once merged.

Sasha: I'll run a canary with ROUTE_SEQ_LEN_THRESHOLD=64 and kernel preference set for one shard to compare metrics. If p99 improves and outputs are close, we can use that as a short-term mitigation.

ci-bot: Created ticket P-4821 "onboard tokenizer remap -> canary p99 regression". Bisect notes: suspect commit 0f3a9b2, tokenizer_map change. Links: http://ci/perf/P-4821

Marco: Quick note — tokenizer remap was introduced to reduce vocab size and improve compression. We need to add a perf/regression test on token-length distribution for future onboards.

Ada: Good point. Add a CI check: avg_token_delta <= 2 tokens on our sample corpus, otherwise flag. I'll follow up in product board.

Lee: After revert PR lands, I'll validate KV cache hit rates and kernel choices across canary fleet. If revert fixes it we can unblock rollout and then propose a migration path that preserves token id locality.

Ada: Thanks all. Keep updates here. If revert/threshold test confirms, we'll unblock the canary tonight. :thumbsup:
